findings.title: VIEW-only group permission grants global group manage
findings.body: canManage() with no group argument returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin granted only the view scope on all Groups passes requireManage(). That check is used, for example, by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup to authorize creating top-level groups, so a read-only FGAP admin can create groups. Unlike canManage(GroupModel), which correctly requires only MANAGE, the global check should not treat VIEW as sufficient.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns and looks up authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: The method passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(), but hasPermission() treats that argument as a group ID and calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). For resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, the resource name is the group ID while getId() is the authorization store's generated resource ID, so the lookup misses and falls back to the all-groups resource. It also adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set, whereas callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount expect real group IDs for the UserModel.GROUPS filter/count. Per-group view-members/manage-members grants can therefore be lost or produce counts/filters that match no group; the resource name (the group ID) should be used in both places.

findings.title: hasPermission can NPE when the all-groups resource does not exist
findings.body: When no specific group resource is found, hasPermission() assigns resource from getResourceTypeResource() and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, and later dereferences resource.getScopes(). getResourceTypeResource() returns null when the Groups type resource has not been created (for example before schema initialization completes or after it is removed), so permission checks such as canView()/canManage() can fail with a NullPointerException/500 instead of returning false/Forbidden.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve Groups resources
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases only the Users resource type: it returns 'All users' and resolves individual user IDs to usernames, but has no corresponding branch for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE. Group policies therefore fall back to resource.getDisplayName(), which for schema-created group resources is the group ID rather than the group name (and never yields an 'All groups' label), so the admin authorization UI/API shows opaque IDs for the newly added Groups resource type.
